{{Verse|3|15}} And I will put enmitie betweene thee and the woman, and betweene thy ſeed and her ſeed: it ſhal bruiſe thy head, and thou ſhalt bruiſe his heele.

{{Verse|3|16}} Unto the woman he ſaid, I will greatly multiply thy ſorowe and thy conception.  In ſorow thou ſhalt bring forth children: and thy deſire {{smaller|ſhall be}} ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=ǁ''Or, ſubiect to thy huſband.''}} to thy huſband, and hee ſhall *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* 1. Corin. 14. 34.}} rule ouer thee.

{{Verse|3|17}} And vnto Adam he ſaid, Becauſe thou haſt hearkened vnto the voyce of thy wife, and haſt eaten of the tree, of which I commaunded thee, ſaying, Thou ſhalt not eate of it: curſed {{smaller|is}} the ground for thy ſake: in ſorow ſhalt thou eate {{smaller|of}} it all the dayes of thy life.

{{Verse|3|18}} Thornes alſo and thiſtles ſhall it †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. cauſe to bud.''}} bring forth to thee: and thou ſhalt eate the herbe of the field.

{{Verse|3|19}} In the ſweate of thy face ſhalt thou eate bread, till thou returne vnto the ground: for out of it waſt thou taken, for duſt thou {{smaller|art}}, and vnto duſt ſhalt thou returne.

{{Verse|3|20}} And Adam called his wiues name †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. Chauah.''}} Eue, becauſe ſhe was the mother of all liuing.

{{Verse|3|21}} Unto Adam alſo, and to his wife, did the LORD God make coates of ſkinnes, and cloathed them.

{{Verse|3|22}} ¶ And the LORD God ſaid, Behold, the man is become as one of vs, to know good ⁊ euill. And now leſt hee put foorth his hand, and take alſo of the tree of life, and eate and liue for euer:

{{Verse|3|23}} Therefore the LORD God ſent him foorth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground, from whence he was taken.

{{Verse|3|24}} So he droue out the man: and he placed at the Eaſt of the garden of Eden, Cherubims, and a 
flaming ſword, which turned euery way, to keepe the way of the tree of life.

{{smaller block|[[#4:1|1]] The birth, trade, and religion of Cain and Abel. [[#4:8|8]] The murder of Abel. [[#4:9|9]] The curſe of Cain. [[#4:17|17]] Enoch the firſt citie. [[#4:19|19]] Lamech and his two wiues. [[#4:25|25]] The birth of Seth, [[#4:26|26]] and Enos.}}

{{Verse|4|1|notext=}} {{dropinitial|A|image=King James Bible (1611) page A1v (A).png|imgsize=100px}}Nd Adam knew Eue his wife, and ſhee conceiued, and bare Cain, and ſaid, I haue gotten a man from the LORD.

{{Verse|4|2}} And ſhe againe bare his brother †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. Hebel.''}} Abel, and Abel was a †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. a feeder.''}} keeper of ſheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

{{Verse|4|3}} And †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. at the end of dayes.''}} in proceſſe of time it came to paſſe, that Cain brought of the fruite of the ground, an offering vnto the LORD.

{{Verse|4|4}} And Abel, he alſo brought of the firſtlings of his †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. ſheep, or goates.''}} flocke, and of the fat thereof: and the LORD had *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* Heb. 11. 4.}} reſpect vnto Abel, and to his offering.

{{Verse|4|5}} But vnto Cain, and to his offring he had not reſpect: and Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.

{{Verse|4|6}} And the LORD ſaid vnto Cain, Why art thou wroth? And why is thy countenance fallen?

{{Verse|4|7}} If thou doe well, ſhalt thou not ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=ǁ''Or, ''haue'' the excellencie?''}} be accepted? and if thou doeſt not well, ſinne lieth at the doore: And ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=ǁ''Or, ſubiect vnto thee.''}} vnto thee {{smaller|ſhall be}} his deſire, and thou ſhalt rule ouer him.

{{Verse|4|8}} And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to paſſe *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* Wiſ. 10. 3 matth. 23. 35. 1. iohn 3. 12. iude 11.}} when they were in the field, that Cain roſe vp againſt Abel his brother, and ſlew him.

{{Verse|4|9}} ¶ And the LORD ſaid vnto Cain, Where {{smaller|is}} Abel thy brother? And hee ſaid, I know not: {{smaller|Am}} I my brothers keeper?

{{Verse|4|10}} And he ſaid, What haſt thou done? the voyce of thy brothers †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. bloods''}} blood cryeth vnto me, from the ground.

{{Verse|4|11}} And now {{smaller|art}} thou curſed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receiue thy brothers blood from thy hand.

{{Verse|4|12}} When thou tilleſt the ground, it ſhall not henceforth yeeld vnto thee her ſtrength: A fugitiue and a vagabond ſhalt thou be in the earth.

{{Verse|4|13}} And Cain ſaid vnto the LORD, ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=ǁ''Or, my iniquitie is greater, then that it may be forgiuen.''}} My puniſhment {{smaller|is}} greater, then I can beare.

{{Verse|4|14}} Behold, thou haſt driuen me out this day from the face of the earth, and from thy face ſhall I be hid, and I ſhall be a fugitiue, and a vagabond in the earth: and it ſhall come to paſſe, {{smaller|that}} euery one that findeth me, ſhall ſlay me.

{{Verse|4|15}} And the LORD ſaid vnto him, Therefore whoſoeuer ſlayeth Cain, vengeance ſhalbe taken on him ſeuen fold.  And the LORD ſet a marke vpon Cain, leſt any finding him, ſhould kill him.

{{Verse|4|16}} ¶ And Cain went out from the preſence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the Eaſt of Eden.
